results.statement: Stocks with the highest trailing 12-month return excluding the most recent month outperform the lowest over the following month.
results.rationale: Jegadeesh-Titman. The skipped month removes short-horizon reversal, which points the other way and otherwise cancels part of the effect. Re-tested inside this family because its earlier standalone run could only be corrected against its own variants.
results.killCriteria: Retire if the Wilson lower bound fails to clear 50% + costs, or if it does not survive FDR across this family.
results.sentence: Wins 56.3% at 21d against a 50.0% base rate. The 95% lower bound is 52.6% on 711 independent observations — clear of the null, so this is allowed to move a decision.

results.statement: 12-1 momentum outperforms when MORE than half the panel trades above its own 200-session average.
results.rationale: Momentum crashes are concentrated in reversals off broad weakness. Breadth measured from the panel itself rather than an index, because an index can be carried by a few mega-caps while most names fall — and it is the many that the short leg holds.
results.killCriteria: Retire if it fails the gate. If BOTH regime halves look like the unconditional result, the tail is not a regime effect and conditioning is not the answer.
results.sentence: Wins 57.7% at 21d against a 50.0% base rate. The 95% lower bound is 53.6% on 579 independent observations — clear of the null, so this is allowed to move a decision.

results.statement: 12-1 momentum outperforms when HALF OR FEWER of the panel trades above its own 200-session average.
results.rationale: The complement, declared so the pair partitions all periods. The prior says this is where momentum should be weakest or negative; if it is instead the stronger half, the received explanation for momentum crashes is wrong on this panel and that is worth knowing.
results.killCriteria: Retire if it fails the gate. A NEGATIVE spread here is a finding rather than a failure — it would locate the crash risk precisely.
results.sentence: Wins 50.0% at 21d against a 50.0% base rate, but the 95% lower bound is 41.6% on 132 independent observations — the interval contains the null, so this is a coin flip as measured.

results.statement: Stocks with the WORST return over the last 5 sessions outperform the best over the following 5 sessions.
results.rationale: Short-horizon reversal from liquidity provision — sharp moves overshoot as market makers demand compensation for absorbing flow. Ranked so the losers score highest, because the claim is that they win. The momentum study's skipped month is indirect evidence this exists.
results.killCriteria: Retire if the spread is not positive, OR if reversal-5d-skip1 fails — passing alone is the signature of a bid-ask bounce rather than information.
results.sentence: Wins 54.0% at 5d against a 50.0% base rate. The 95% lower bound is 52.2% on 3037 independent observations — clear of the null, so this is allowed to move a decision.

results.statement: The 5-day reversal effect survives when entry is delayed one session after the signal.
results.rationale: THE FALSIFICATION TEST for reversal-5d, declared before either was run. Close-to-close reversal at short horizons is substantially bid-ask bounce: a stock closing on the bid and then on the ask shows a reversal nobody could trade. Delaying entry one session steps over the bounce. If reversal-5d survives and this does not, the effect was microstructure and neither is tradeable.
results.killCriteria: If this fails while reversal-5d passes, BOTH are retired — that pattern is the signature of a bounce artifact, and shipping the unskipped version would be shipping a spread that only exists between the quotes.
results.sentence: Wins 52.9% at 5d against a 50.0% base rate, but the 95% lower bound is 51.1% on 3037 independent observations — the interval contains the null, so this is a coin flip as measured.

results.statement: Stocks trading closest to their 52-week high outperform those furthest below it over the following month.
results.rationale: George & Hwang: the 52-week high acts as an anchor, and traders under-react to news that pushes price through it. Distinct from momentum — a stock can be near its high without a large trailing return.
results.killCriteria: Retire if it fails the gate, or if it survives only where momentum also survives — that would make it a momentum proxy rather than its own signal.
results.sentence: Wins 49.2% at 21d against a 50.0% base rate — below the null on 711 independent observations. Doing nothing beat it.

results.statement: Stocks whose 20-session realised volatility is lowest relative to their own 60-session volatility outperform over the following month.
results.rationale: Volatility clusters and mean-reverts. A contracted stock is either coiling before expansion or genuinely de-risking; the claim is that the average outcome is favourable. Ratio rather than level, so the ranking is not a proxy for 'low-beta stocks'.
results.killCriteria: Retire if the spread is not positive. A negative spread would mean expansion is the tradeable side and should be declared as its own hypothesis, not this one with a flipped sign.
results.sentence: Wins 52.1% at 21d against a 50.0% base rate, but the 95% lower bound is 48.4% on 720 independent observations — the interval contains the null, so this is a coin flip as measured.

results.statement: Stocks whose 5-session average volume most exceeds their 60-session average outperform over the following month.
results.rationale: Volume expansion marks the arrival of informed flow, and price tends to follow participation. The weakest form of the family's ideas and included precisely so a null result is on the record.
results.killCriteria: Retire if it fails the gate. Volume without direction is the most likely of these to be pure noise.
results.sentence: Wins 54.0% at 21d against a 50.0% base rate, but the 95% lower bound is 50.4% on 720 independent observations — the interval contains the null, so this is a coin flip as measured.

results.statement: Stocks with the highest 12-1 momentum PER UNIT of realised volatility outperform the lowest over the following month.
results.rationale: Raw momentum loads on high-volatility names, so part of its spread may be a volatility premium rather than momentum. Dividing by 60-session volatility asks whether the effect survives once that loading is removed. Declared alongside raw momentum specifically so the comparison is corrected, not chosen.
results.killCriteria: Retire if it fails the gate. If it survives where raw momentum does not, the honest reading is that the volatility scaling — not momentum — is doing the work, and that must be said.
results.sentence: Wins 57.0% at 21d against a 50.0% base rate. The 95% lower bound is 53.3% on 711 independent observations — clear of the null, so this is allowed to move a decision.
